title: Jeremiah

stories.title: 🌿 Jeremiah 1
summaryBullets: These are the words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests in Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin. (1:1).
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in the thirteenth year of the reign of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah, (1:2).
and through the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, until the fifth month of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah king of Judah, when the people of Jerusalem went into exile. (1:3).
The word of the LORD came to me, saying: (1:4).
“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I set you apart and appointed you as a prophet to the nations.” (1:5).
“Ah, Lord GOD,” I said, “I surely do not know how to speak, for I am only a child!” (1:6).
But the LORD told me: “Do not say, ‘I am only a child.’ For to everyone I send you, you must go, and all that I command you, you must speak. (1:7).
Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you,” declares the LORD. (1:8).
Then the LORD reached out His hand, touched my mouth, and said to me: “Behold, I have put My words in your mouth. (1:9).
See, I have appointed you today over nations and kingdoms to uproot and tear down, to destroy and overthrow, to build and plant.” (1:10).
And the word of the LORD came to me, asking, “Jeremiah, what do you see?” “I see a branch of an almond tree,” I replied. (1:11).
“You have observed correctly,” said the LORD, “for I am watching over My word to accomplish it.” (1:12).
Again the word of the LORD came to me, asking, “What do you see?” “I see a boiling pot,” I replied, “and it is tilting toward us from the north.” (1:13).
Then the LORD said to me, “Disaster from the north will be poured out on all who live in the land. (1:14).

For I am about to summon all the clans and kingdoms of the north,” declares the LORD. “Their kings will come and set up their thrones at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem. They will attack all her surrounding walls and all the other cities of Judah. (1:15).
I will pronounce My judgments against them for all their wickedness, because they have forsaken Me, and they have burned incense to other gods and worshiped the works of their own hands. (1:16).
Get yourself ready. Stand up and tell them everything that I command you. Do not be intimidated by them, or I will terrify you before them. (1:17).

Now behold, this day I have made you like a fortified city, an iron pillar, and bronze walls against the whole land— against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests, and the people of the land. (1:18).
They will fight against you but will never overcome you, since I am with you to deliver you,” declares the LORD. (1:19).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 22:1-23:25: Josiah's reign and reforms, the setting Jeremiah is called into in 1:2.
Exodus 4:10-12: Moses objects that he cannot speak, and is told who made the mouth.
Amos 7:14-15: A prophet with no prophetic training says the LORD took him from following the flock.
Isaiah 49:1: The LORD called me from the womb and named me before I was born.
Jeremiah 20:9: The word becomes a fire shut up in his bones that he cannot hold in, the commission of 1:9 under strain.

translationNotes.note: A spokesman authorized to deliver God's words, not a fortune teller. The office carried legal weight: Deuteronomy 18:20-22 makes a prophet answerable with his life for words the LORD did not command, and gives fulfilment as the test.

Jeremiah dates his oracles by the regnal year of the reigning king, the standard way of fixing a date before there were era calendars. Josiah reigned about 640 to 609 BC, so his thirteenth year is about 627 BC. Verse 3 runs the span to the eleventh year of Zedekiah, about 586 BC, giving Jeremiah roughly forty years of preaching.

Jeremiah's home town, a priestly settlement in Benjamin about three miles (5 km) northeast of Jerusalem, close enough to see the city. Joshua 21:18 lists it among the towns given to the priests, and 1 Kings 2:26 is where Solomon banished the priest Abiathar to his fields there. Jeremiah is a priest's son writing from a priests' town, which is why the men of Anathoth plotting against him in 11:21 are his own neighbours and kin.

The almond branch and the verb for keeping watch are nearly the same word in Hebrew. The almond is the first tree in the land to blossom, in late winter before its leaves come, so it is the tree that wakes early. English cannot carry the pun, which is why the answer in 1:12 sounds unconnected to the question.

Armies out of Mesopotamia never came straight west across the Arabian desert. They followed the Euphrates up and around the Fertile Crescent and came down through Syria into Israel from above, so Babylon always arrives from the north even though Babylon lies east.

translationNotes.term: Uproot and tear down, build and plant
translationNotes.note: Six verbs set the shape of the whole book: four of demolition, two of rebuilding. The pair returns at 18:7-10, 24:6, 31:28 and 42:10, so the reader can track a single commission running the length of Jeremiah.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jeremiah is called and authorized as a prophet to confront Judah and nations; God shows him the northern threat and promises protection.

stories.title: 💧 Jeremiah 2
summaryBullets: Now the word of the LORD came to me, saying, (2:1).

“Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem that this is what the LORD says: ‘I remember the devotion of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed Me in the wilderness, in a land not sown. (2:2).
Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of His harvest. All who devoured her were found guilty; disaster came upon them,’” declares the LORD. (2:3).
Hear the word of the LORD, O house of Jacob, and all you families of the house of Israel. (2:4).
This is what the LORD says: “What fault did your fathers find in Me that they strayed so far from Me? They followed worthless idols, and became worthless themselves. (2:5).

They did not ask, ‘Where is the LORD who brought us up from the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and pits, a land of drought and darkness, a land where no one travels and no one lives?’ (2:6).
I brought you into a fertile land to eat its fruit and bounty, but you came and defiled My land and made My inheritance detestable. (2:7).
The priests did not ask, ‘Where is the LORD?’ The experts in the law no longer knew Me, and the leaders rebelled against Me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed useless idols. (2:8).
Therefore, I will contend with you again, declares the LORD, and I will bring a case against your children’s children. (2:9).
Cross over to the coasts of Cyprus and take a look; send to Kedar and consider carefully; see if there has ever been anything like this: (2:10).
Has a nation ever changed its gods? (Yet they are not gods at all.) But My people have exchanged their Glory for useless idols. (2:11).
Be stunned by this, O heavens; be shocked and utterly appalled,” declares the LORD. (2:12).
“For My people have committed two evils: They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living water, and they have dug their own cisterns — broken cisterns that cannot hold water. (2:13).
Is Israel a slave? Was he born into slavery? Why then has he become prey? (2:14).
The young lions have roared at him; they have sounded their voices. They have laid waste his land; his cities lie in ruins, without inhabitant. (2:15).
The men of Memphis and Tahpanhes have shaved the crown of your head. (2:16).
Have you not brought this on yourself by forsaking the LORD your God when He led you in the way? (2:17).
Now what will you gain on your way to Egypt to drink the waters of the Nile? What will you gain on your way to Assyria to drink the waters of the Euphrates? (2:18).

Your own evil will discipline you; your own apostasies will reprimand you. Consider and realize how evil and bitter it is for you to forsake the LORD your God and to have no fear of Me,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts. (2:19).
“For long ago you broke your yoke and tore off your chains, saying, ‘I will not serve!’ Indeed, on every high hill and under every green tree you lay down as a prostitute. (2:20).
I had planted you like a choice vine from the very best seed. How could you turn yourself before Me into a rotten, wild vine? (2:21).
Although you wash with lye and use an abundance of soap, the stain of your guilt is still before Me,” declares the Lord GOD. (2:22).

“How can you say, ‘I am not defiled; I have not run after the Baals’? Look at your behavior in the valley; acknowledge what you have done. You are a swift young she-camel galloping here and there, (2:23).

a wild donkey at home in the wilderness, sniffing the wind in the heat of her desire. Who can restrain her passion? All who seek her need not weary themselves; in mating season they will find her. (2:24).
You should have kept your feet from going bare and your throat from being thirsty. But you said, ‘It is hopeless! For I love foreign gods, and I must go after them.’ (2:25).
As the thief is ashamed when he is caught, so the house of Israel is disgraced. They, their kings, their officials, their priests, and their prophets (2:26).
say to a tree, ‘You are my father,’ and to a stone, ‘You gave me birth.’ They have turned their backs to Me and not their faces. Yet in the time of trouble, they say, ‘Rise up and save us!’ (2:27).
But where are the gods you made for yourselves? Let them rise up in your time of trouble and save you if they can; for your gods are as numerous as your cities, O Judah. (2:28).
Why do you bring a case against Me? You have all rebelled against Me,” declares the LORD. (2:29).
“I have struck your sons in vain; they accepted no discipline. Your own sword has devoured your prophets like a voracious lion.” (2:30).

You people of this generation, consider the word of the LORD: “Have I been a wilderness to Israel or a land of dense darkness? Why do My people say, ‘We are free to roam; we will come to You no more’? (2:31).
Does a maiden forget her jewelry or a bride her wedding sash? Yet My people have forgotten Me for days without number. (2:32).
How skillfully you pursue love! Even the most immoral of women could learn from your ways. (2:33).
Moreover, your skirts are stained with the blood of the innocent poor, though you did not find them breaking in. But in spite of all these things (2:34).
you say, ‘I am innocent. Surely His anger will turn from me.’ Behold, I will judge you, because you say, ‘I have not sinned.’ (2:35).
How impulsive you are, constantly changing your ways! You will be disappointed by Egypt just as you were by Assyria. (2:36).
Moreover, you will leave that place with your hands on your head, for the LORD has rejected those you trust; you will not prosper by their help.” (2:37).
crossRefs: Exodus 20:3-5: The command against other gods and carved images, with the LORD naming Himself jealous.
Deuteronomy 32:15-18: Israel grows fat, forsakes the Rock who made him, and sacrifices to gods that were no gods.
Isaiah 1:2-4: The LORD calls heaven and earth as witnesses against sons who have forsaken Him.
Isaiah 30:1-3: Going down to Egypt for help is called a refuge that turns to shame.
2 Kings 17:7-17: The reasons given for the northern kingdom's exile, idolatry and foreign alliances together.

translationNotes.note: A bottle-shaped shaft cut down into bedrock, narrow at the mouth so a lid or a stone could cover it, widening into a chamber below, and lined with lime plaster because Judean limestone leaks. It caught winter runoff from a roof or a channel and held it through the dry months. Crack the plaster and the whole thing empties into the rock, which is exactly the failure 2:13 describes.

The Hebrew for spring water is literally living water: water that moves and renews itself. A cistern holds still water that goes stale and breeds. The charge in 2:13 is a double one, trading a spring for a tank, and then for a tank that does not even hold.
The word means vapour or breath, the same word translated vanity throughout Ecclesiastes. Idols are called breath, and 2:5 turns it on the worshippers: they went after breath and became breath.

A fixed phrase for open-air Canaanite shrines, which were sited on ridge tops and beside large trees rather than in buildings. Deuteronomy 12:2 orders these places destroyed by name. The worship at them was fertility worship, which is why 2:20 and 2:23-25 describe it in sexual terms.

The two great powers Judah kept playing against each other. Drinking the waters of the Nile and of the River in 2:18 means buying protection from Egypt in the south or Assyria in the north. Judah did both in turn, and 2 Kings 16 and 18 record what each alliance cost.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells Jeremiah to remind Jerusalem that he remembers their early devotion, but they have abandoned him for worthless idols, defiled his land, and killed innocent people; he will judge them because they refuse correction and trust in foreign nations instead of him.

stories.title: 💧 Jeremiah 3
summaryBullets: “If a man divorces his wife and she leaves him to marry another, can he ever return to her? Would not such a land be completely defiled? But you have played the harlot with many lovers — and you would return to Me?” declares the LORD. (3:1).

“Lift up your eyes to the barren heights and see. Is there any place where you have not been violated? You sat beside the highways waiting for your lovers, like a nomad in the desert. You have defiled the land with your prostitution and wickedness. (3:2).
Therefore the showers have been withheld, and no spring rains have fallen. Yet you have the brazen look of a prostitute; you refuse to be ashamed. (3:3).
Have you not just called to Me, ‘My Father, You are my friend from youth. (3:4).
Will He be angry forever? Will He be indignant to the end?’ This you have spoken, but you keep doing all the evil you can.” (3:5).
Now in the days of King Josiah, the LORD said to me, “Have you seen what faithless Israel has done? She has gone up on every high hill and under every green tree to prostitute herself there. (3:6).
I thought that after she had done all these things, she would return to Me. But she did not return, and her unfaithful sister Judah saw it. (3:7).

She saw that because faithless Israel had committed adultery, I gave her a certificate of divorce and sent her away. Yet that unfaithful sister Judah had no fear and prostituted herself as well. (3:8).
Indifferent to her own infidelity, Israel had defiled the land and committed adultery with stones and trees. (3:9).
Yet in spite of all this, her unfaithful sister Judah did not return to Me with all her heart, but only in pretense,” declares the LORD. (3:10).
And the LORD said to me, “Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than unfaithful Judah. (3:11).

Go, proclaim this message toward the north: ‘Return, O faithless Israel,’ declares the LORD. ‘I will no longer look on you with anger, for I am merciful,’ declares the LORD. ‘I will not be angry forever. (3:12).

Only acknowledge your guilt, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God. You have scattered your favors to foreign gods under every green tree and have not obeyed My voice,’” declares the LORD. (3:13).
“Return, O faithless children,” declares the LORD, “for I am your master, and I will take you — one from a city and two from a family — and bring you to Zion. (3:14).
Then I will give you shepherds after My own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.” (3:15).

“In those days, when you multiply and increase in the land,” declares the LORD, “they will no longer discuss the ark of the covenant of the LORD. It will never come to mind, and no one will remember it or miss it, nor will another one be made. (3:16).

At that time they will call Jerusalem The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations will be gathered in Jerusalem to honor the name of the LORD. They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts. (3:17).
In those days the house of Judah will walk with the house of Israel, and they will come together from the land of the north to the land that I gave to your fathers as an inheritance. (3:18).

Then I said, ‘How I long to make you My sons and give you a desirable land, the most beautiful inheritance of all the nations!’ I thought you would call Me ‘Father’ and never turn away from following Me. (3:19).
But as a woman may betray her husband, so you have betrayed Me, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD. (3:20).
A voice is heard on the barren heights, the children of Israel weeping and begging for mercy, because they have perverted their ways and forgotten the LORD their God. (3:21).
“Return, O faithless children, and I will heal your faithlessness.” “Here we are. We come to You, for You are the LORD our God. (3:22).
Surely deception comes from the hills, and commotion from the mountains. Surely the salvation of Israel is in the LORD our God. (3:23).
From our youth, that shameful god has consumed what our fathers have worked for— their flocks and herds, their sons and daughters. (3:24).

Let us lie down in our shame; let our disgrace cover us. We have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our fathers; from our youth even to this day we have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God.” (3:25).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 24:1-4: The law forbidding a man to take back a wife he divorced after she has married another; the case 3:1 opens with.
2 Kings 17:6-18: Israel carried off to Assyria, the divorce 3:8 says Judah watched and ignored.
Hosea 3:1-5: Hosea is told to love an adulterous wife again, and Israel afterward seeks the LORD.
Deuteronomy 30:1-5: Return promised from the farthest place when the scattered people turn back with all their heart.
Jeremiah 23:3-4: Shepherds promised who will feed the flock, the same pledge as 3:15.

translationNotes.note: One Hebrew verb runs through this chapter meaning turn, turn back, return, and repent. It appears more than a dozen times in 3:1-22, including the pun in 3:22 where the LORD tells backsliding sons to turn back and He will heal their turning. English needs several different words and loses the drumbeat.

Deuteronomy 24:1-4 forbids a man to remarry a wife he divorced once she has been another man's wife; the land itself is said to be polluted by it. The chapter opens by quoting that statute, so the offer of return that follows is offered against a law that says it cannot be done.

The two kingdoms get two different labels. Israel, the northern ten tribes taken by Assyria in 722 BC, is called Turning-Away. Judah, the southern kingdom still standing as Jeremiah speaks, is called Treachery, and 3:11 says the one that watched and learned nothing is the worse of the two.

The gold-plated chest holding the tablets of the law, kept in the innermost room of the temple and seen by the high priest alone, one day a year. Saying in 3:16 that it will not be missed or remade is a statement no one in Jerusalem would have heard calmly.

stories.keyTakeaway: God compares Judah's idolatry to marital unfaithfulness and offers restoration if they acknowledge their guilt and return; Israel's weeping people respond that they will come back to the LORD as their God.

stories.title: 🧭 Jeremiah 4
summaryBullets: “If you will return, O Israel, return to Me,” declares the LORD. “If you will remove your detestable idols from My sight and no longer waver, (4:1).
and if you can swear, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ in truth, in justice, and in righteousness, then the nations will be blessed by Him, and in Him they will glory.” (4:2).
For this is what the LORD says to the men of Judah and Jerusalem: “Break up your unplowed ground, and do not sow among the thorns. (4:3).

Circumcise yourselves to the LORD, and remove the foreskins of your hearts, O men of Judah and people of Jerusalem. Otherwise, My wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to extinguish it, because of your evil deeds.” (4:4).
Announce in Judah, proclaim in Jerusalem, and say: “Blow the ram’s horn throughout the land. Cry aloud and say, ‘Assemble yourselves and let us flee to the fortified cities.’ (4:5).
Raise a signal flag toward Zion. Seek refuge! Do not delay! For I am bringing disaster from the north, and terrible destruction. (4:6).
A lion has gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his lair to lay waste your land. Your cities will be reduced to ruins and lie uninhabited. (4:7).
So put on sackcloth, mourn and wail, for the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.” (4:8).
“In that day,” declares the LORD, “the king and officials will lose their courage. The priests will tremble in fear, and the prophets will be astounded.” (4:9).
Then I said, “Ah, Lord GOD, how completely You have deceived this people and Jerusalem by saying, ‘You will have peace,’ while a sword is at our throats.” (4:10).
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem, “A searing wind from the barren heights in the desert blows toward the daughter of My people, but not to winnow or to sift; (4:11).
a wind too strong for that comes from Me. Now I also pronounce judgments against them.” (4:12).
Behold, he advances like the clouds, his chariots like the whirlwind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined! (4:13).
Wash the evil from your heart, O Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will you harbor wicked thoughts within you? (4:14).
For a voice resounds from Dan, proclaiming disaster from the hills of Ephraim. (4:15).
Warn the nations now! Proclaim to Jerusalem: “A besieging army comes from a distant land; they raise their voices against the cities of Judah. (4:16).
They surround her like men guarding a field, because she has rebelled against Me,” declares the LORD. (4:17).
“Your ways and deeds have brought this upon you. This is your punishment; how bitter it is, because it pierces to the heart!” (4:18).
My anguish, my anguish! I writhe in pain! Oh, the pain in my chest! My heart pounds within me; I cannot be silent. For I have heard the sound of the horn, the alarm of battle. (4:19).
Disaster after disaster is proclaimed, for the whole land is laid waste. My tents are destroyed in an instant, my curtains in a moment. (4:20).
How long must I see the signal flag and hear the sound of the horn? (4:21).
“For My people are fools; they have not known Me. They are foolish children, without understanding. They are skilled in doing evil, but they know not how to do good.” (4:22).
I looked at the earth, and it was formless and void; I looked to the heavens, and they had no light. (4:23).
I looked at the mountains, and behold, they were quaking; all the hills were swaying. (4:24).
I looked, and no man was left; all the birds of the air had fled. (4:25).
I looked, and the fruitful land was a desert. All its cities were torn down before the LORD, before His fierce anger. (4:26).
For this is what the LORD says: “The whole land will be desolate, but I will not finish its destruction. (4:27).
Therefore the earth will mourn and the heavens above will grow dark. I have spoken, I have planned, and I will not relent or turn back.” (4:28).
Every city flees at the sound of the horseman and archer. They enter the thickets and climb among the rocks. Every city is abandoned; no inhabitant is left. (4:29).

And you, O devastated one, what will you do, though you dress yourself in scarlet, though you adorn yourself with gold jewelry, though you enlarge your eyes with paint? You adorn yourself in vain; your lovers despise you; they want to take your life. (4:30).

For I hear a cry like a woman in labor, a cry of anguish like one bearing her first child — the cry of the Daughter of Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands to say, “Woe is me, for my soul faints before the murderers!” (4:31).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 10:16: Circumcise the foreskin of your heart and be stiff-necked no longer.
Genesis 1:2: The earth formless and empty, the phrase 4:23 reuses to describe the land after judgment.
2 Kings 25:1-10: Babylon's siege and the burning of Jerusalem, the northern threat arriving.
Hosea 14:1-2: A call to return to the LORD with words of confession in hand.
Joel 2:12-13: Rend your heart and not your garments, the same demand for inward turning.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שׁוּב (shuv, ‘turn/return’), Greek (LXX): ἐπιστρέφω, Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): תוב (tuv)
translationNotes.note: Key covenant verb for repentance in 3:12-14.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: הִמּוֹלוּ… וְהָסִירוּ עָרְלוֹת לְבַבְכֶם (himmōlu… ve-hāsīru ʿorlot levavkhem), Greek: περιτμήθητε… ἀφελεῖτε τὰς ἀκροβυστίας τῆς καρδίας, Aramaic: אִתְגְּזֹרוּ… סַקּוּ עָרְלָא דְלִבְכֹון
translationNotes.note: Figure for removing inner hardness (4:4).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ (tohu va-bohu), Greek: ἀόρατος καὶ ἀκατασκεύαστος, Aramaic: תוהו ובוהו
translationNotes.note: Creation-chaos phrase reused to depict Judah’s devastation (4:23).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: מִצָּפוֹן (mi-ṣāfōn), Greek: ἀπὸ βορρᾶ, Aramaic: מן צפונא
translationNotes.note: Route of Mesopotamian invasion into Judah (4:6).

A coarse, dark goat-hair fabric worn against bare skin as a universal sign of mourning, repentance, or distress (1 Kings 21:27; Jonah 3:5; Matthew 11:21). Wearing it publicly broadcast grief or contrition; the discomfort itself was part of the symbolism.

stories.keyTakeaway: Judah is urged to return with a changed heart as a northern invader approaches; Jeremiah sees near-total ruin if they refuse.

stories.title: 🔎 Jeremiah 5
summaryBullets: “Go up and down the streets of Jerusalem. Look now and take note; search her squares. If you can find a single person, anyone who acts justly, anyone who seeks the truth, then I will forgive the city. (5:1).
Although they say, ‘As surely as the LORD lives,’ they are swearing falsely.” (5:2).

O LORD, do not Your eyes look for truth? You struck them, but they felt no pain. You finished them off, but they refused to accept discipline. They have made their faces harder than stone and refused to repent. (5:3).
Then I said, “They are only the poor; they have played the fool, for they do not know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God. (5:4).
I will go to the powerful and speak to them. Surely they know the way of the LORD, the justice of their God.” But they too, with one accord, had broken the yoke and torn off the chains. (5:5).

Therefore a lion from the forest will strike them down, a wolf from the desert will ravage them. A leopard will lie in wait near their cities, and everyone who ventures out will be torn to pieces. For their rebellious acts are many, and their unfaithful deeds are numerous. (5:6).
“Why should I forgive you? Your children have forsaken Me and sworn by gods that are not gods. I satisfied their needs, yet they committed adultery and assembled at the houses of prostitutes. (5:7).
They are well-fed, lusty stallions, each neighing after his neighbor’s wife. (5:8).
Should I not punish them for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this? (5:9).
Go up through her vineyards and ravage them, but do not finish them off. Strip off her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD. (5:10).
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been utterly unfaithful to Me,” declares the LORD. (5:11).
They have lied about the LORD and said: “He will not do anything; harm will not come to us; we will not see sword or famine. (5:12).
The prophets are but wind, for the word is not in them. So let their own predictions befall them.” (5:13).
Therefore this is what the LORD God of Hosts says: “Because you have spoken this word, I will make My words a fire in your mouth and this people the wood it consumes. (5:14).

Behold, I am bringing a distant nation against you, O house of Israel,” declares the LORD. “It is an established nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you do not understand. (5:15).
Their quivers are like open graves; they are all mighty men. (5:16).

They will devour your harvest and food; they will consume your sons and daughters; they will eat up your flocks and herds; they will feed on your vines and fig trees. With the sword they will destroy the fortified cities in which you trust.” (5:17).
“Yet even in those days,” declares the LORD, “I will not make a full end of you. (5:18).

And when the people ask, ‘For what offense has the LORD our God done all these things to us?’ You are to tell them, ‘Just as you have forsaken Me and served foreign gods in your land, so will you serve foreigners in a land that is not your own.’” (5:19).
Declare this in the house of Jacob and proclaim it in Judah: (5:20).
“Hear this, O foolish and senseless people, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear. (5:21).

Do you not fear Me?” declares the LORD. “Do you not tremble before Me, the One who set the sand as the boundary for the sea, an enduring barrier it cannot cross? The waves surge, but they cannot prevail. They roar but cannot cross it. (5:22).
But these people have stubborn and rebellious hearts. They have turned aside and gone away. (5:23).
They have not said in their hearts, ‘Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rains, both autumn and spring, in season, who keeps for us the appointed weeks of harvest.’ (5:24).
Your iniquities have diverted these from you; your sins have deprived you of My bounty. (5:25).
For among My people are wicked men; they watch like fowlers lying in wait; they set a trap to catch men. (5:26).
Like cages full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Therefore they have become powerful and rich. (5:27).

They have grown fat and sleek, and have excelled in the deeds of the wicked. They have not taken up the cause of the fatherless, that they might prosper; nor have they defended the rights of the needy. (5:28).
Should I not punish them for these things?” declares the LORD. “Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this? (5:29).
A horrible and shocking thing has happened in the land. (5:30).
The prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule by their own authority. My people love it so, but what will you do in the end? (5:31).
crossRefs: Deuteronomy 28:49-52: A nation brought from far away whose language you do not understand, in the covenant curses.
Genesis 18:23-32: Abraham asks whether a city will be spared for the sake of a few righteous men in it.
Amos 5:14-15: Seek good and not evil, and establish justice in the gate.
Micah 3:5-11: Prophets, priests and rulers all working for money while leaning on the LORD.
Isaiah 5:1-7: God looks for justice in His vineyard and finds bloodshed, and for righteousness and hears an outcry.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: לֹא עָשָׂה כָלָה (lo ʿasah kalah), Greek (LXX): οὐ ποιήσω συντέλειαν, Aramaic (Tg./Syr.): לָא אֶעֱבֵיד כָּלָה
translationNotes.note: Refrain of limited judgment (5:10-18).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נִבְּאוּ בַשֶּׁקֶר (nibbeʾu ba-sheqer), Greek (LXX): ἐπροφήτευσαν ἐν ψεύδει, Aramaic: אתנביוּ בכזבא
translationNotes.note: Charge against prophets giving false messages (5:31).

translationNotes.term: Priests rule by their own authority
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: וְהַכֹּהֲנִים יִרְדּוּ עַל־יְדֵיהֶם (ha-kohanim yirdū ʿal-yedehem), Greek (LXX): οἱ ἱερεῖς ἐπικρατοῦσιν διὰ χειρῶν, Aramaic: כַּהֲנַיָּא שולְטִין בִּידֵיהוֹן
translationNotes.note: Idiomatic phrase: priests exercise power ‘by their hands’, i.e., by their own control (5:31).

stories.keyTakeaway: Jerusalem is exposed as corrupt from top to bottom; judgment is coming by a foreign nation, yet not a total wipeout.

stories.title: 📣 Jeremiah 6
summaryBullets: “Run for cover, O sons of Benjamin; flee from Jerusalem! Sound the ram’s horn in Tekoa; send up a signal over Beth-haccherem, for disaster looms from the north, even great destruction. (6:1).
Though she is beautiful and delicate, I will destroy the Daughter of Zion. (6:2).
Shepherds and their flocks will come against her; they will pitch their tents all around her, each tending his own portion: (6:3).
‘Prepare for battle against her; rise up, let us attack at noon. Woe to us, for the daylight is fading; the evening shadows grow long. (6:4).
Rise up, let us attack by night and destroy her fortresses!’” (6:5).
For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Cut down the trees and raise a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This city must be punished; there is nothing but oppression in her midst. (6:6).
As a well gushes its water, so she pours out her evil. Violence and destruction resound in her; sickness and wounds are ever before Me. (6:7).
Be forewarned, O Jerusalem, or I will turn away from you; I will make you a desolation, a land without inhabitant.” (6:8).
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Glean the remnant of Israel as thoroughly as a vine. Pass your hand once more like a grape gatherer over the branches.” (6:9).
To whom can I give this warning? Who will listen to me? Look, their ears are closed, so they cannot hear. See, the word of the LORD has become offensive to them; they find no pleasure in it. (6:10).

But I am full of the LORD’s wrath; I am tired of holding it back. “Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the young men gathered together. For both husband and wife will be captured, the old and the very old alike. (6:11).
Their houses will be turned over to others, their fields and wives as well, for I will stretch out My hand against the inhabitants of the land,” declares the LORD. (6:12).
“For from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit. (6:13).
They dress the wound of My people with very little care, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace at all. (6:14).

Are they ashamed of the abomination they have committed? No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I punish them, they will collapse,” says the LORD. (6:15).

This is what the LORD says: “Stand at the crossroads and look. Ask for the ancient paths: ‘Where is the good way?’ Then walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls. But they said, ‘We will not walk in it!’ (6:16).
I appointed watchmen over you and said, ‘Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn.’ But they answered, ‘We will not listen!’ (6:17).
Therefore hear, O nations, and learn, O congregations, what will happen to them. (6:18).
Hear, O earth! I am bringing disaster on this people, the fruit of their own schemes, because they have paid no attention to My word and have rejected My instruction. (6:19).
What use to Me is frankincense from Sheba or sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me.” (6:20).
Therefore this is what the LORD says: “I will lay stumbling blocks before this people; fathers and sons alike will be staggered; friends and neighbors will perish.” (6:21).
This is what the LORD says: “Behold, an army is coming from the land of the north; a great nation is stirred up from the ends of the earth. (6:22).
They grasp the bow and spear; they are cruel and merciless. Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, lined up like men in formation against you, O Daughter of Zion.” (6:23).
We have heard the report; our hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped us, pain like that of a woman in labor. (6:24).
Do not go out to the fields; do not walk the road. For the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side. (6:25).
O daughter of my people, dress yourselves in sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn with bitter wailing, as you would for an only son, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us. (6:26).
“I have appointed you to examine My people like ore, so you may know and try their ways. (6:27).
All are hardened rebels, walking around as slanderers. They are bronze and iron; all of them are corrupt. (6:28).
The bellows blow fiercely, blasting away the lead with fire. The refining proceeds in vain, for the wicked are not purged. (6:29).
They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.” (6:30).
crossRefs: Isaiah 1:11-17: Sacrifices refused while hands are full of blood, with the remedy given as doing justice.
Ezekiel 13:10-16: A flimsy wall daubed with whitewash, and the storm that brings it down.
Deuteronomy 20:19-20: Which trees may be cut for siege works and which must be left standing.
Jeremiah 8:10-12: The same lines about greed and about crying peace where there is no peace, repeated word for word.
Malachi 3:2-3: A refiner sitting over the silver until it is purified, the smelting Jeremiah says failed in 6:27-30.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: נְתִיבוֹת עוֹלָם / דֶּרֶךְ הַטּוֹב (netivot ʿolam / derekh ha-tov), Greek (LXX): τρίβοι αἰώνιοι / ὁδὸς ἀγαθή, Aramaic: שבילֵי עָלְמָא / אורח טב
translationNotes.note: Call to return to long-established ways of covenant faithfulness (6:16).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: שָׁלוֹם שָׁלוֹם (shalom shalom), Greek (LXX): εἰρήνη εἰρήνη, Aramaic: שלמא שלמא
translationNotes.note: False assurance that everything is fine (6:14).

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: כֶּסֶף נִמְאָס (kesef nimʾas), Greek (LXX): ἀργύριον ἀπώσθη, Aramaic: כספא מסיא
translationNotes.note: Smelting image: the ore yields no true metal, people refuse to be purified (6:30).

A coarse, dark goat-hair fabric worn against bare skin as a universal sign of mourning, repentance, or distress (1 Kings 21:27; Jonah 3:5; Matthew 11:21). Wearing it publicly broadcast grief or contrition; the discomfort itself was part of the symbolism.

A milky-white resin from the Boswellia tree of southern Arabia. Burned as incense in the temple (Exodus 30:34); offered with every grain offering. The magi's second gift, traditionally read as signaling priesthood.

stories.keyTakeaway: Judah refuses the good way and covers rot with fake ‘peace.’ A northern siege is coming; God rejects empty worship.

stories.title: 🕍 Jeremiah 7
summaryBullets: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying, (7:1).
“Stand in the gate of the house of the LORD and proclaim this message: Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who enter through these gates to worship the LORD. (7:2).
Thus says the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel: Correct your ways and deeds, and I will let you live in this place. (7:3).
Do not trust in deceptive words, saying: ‘This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD.’ (7:4).
For if you really correct your ways and deeds, if you act justly toward one another, (7:5).
if you no longer oppress the foreigner and the fatherless and the widow, and if you no longer shed innocent blood in this place or follow other gods to your own harm, (7:6).
then I will let you live in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers forever and ever. (7:7).
But look, you keep trusting in deceptive words to no avail. (7:8).
Will you steal and murder, commit adultery and perjury, burn incense to Baal, and follow other gods that you have not known, (7:9).
and then come and stand before Me in this house, which bears My Name, and say, ‘We are delivered, so we can continue with all these abominations’? (7:10).
Has this house, which bears My Name, become a den of robbers in your sight? Yes, I too have seen it, declares the LORD. (7:11).
But go now to the place in Shiloh where I first made a dwelling for My Name, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of My people Israel. (7:12).

And now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD, and because I have spoken to you again and again but you would not listen, and I have called to you but you would not answer, (7:13).
therefore what I did to Shiloh I will now do to the house that bears My Name, the house in which you trust, the place that I gave to you and your fathers. (7:14).
And I will cast you out of My presence, just as I have cast out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim. (7:15).
As for you, do not pray for these people, do not offer a plea or petition on their behalf, and do not beg Me, for I will not listen to you. (7:16).
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem? (7:17).
The sons gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead the dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven; they pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke Me to anger. (7:18).
But am I the One they are provoking? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves they spite, to their own shame? (7:19).

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Behold, My anger and My fury will be poured out on this place, on man and beast, on the trees of the field and the produce of the land, and it will burn and not be extinguished. (7:20).
This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: Add your burnt offerings to your other sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves! (7:21).
For when I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt, I did not merely command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices, (7:22).
but this is what I commanded them: Obey Me, and I will be your God, and you will be My people. You must walk in all the ways I have commanded you, so that it may go well with you. (7:23).
Yet they did not listen or incline their ear, but they followed the stubborn inclinations of their own evil hearts. They went backward and not forward. (7:24).
From the day your fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I have sent you all My servants the prophets again and again. (7:25).
Yet they would not listen to Me or incline their ear, but they stiffened their necks and did more evil than their fathers. (7:26).
When you tell them all these things, they will not listen to you. When you call to them, they will not answer. (7:27).

Therefore you must say to them, ‘This is the nation that would not listen to the voice of the LORD their God and would not receive correction. Truth has perished; it has disappeared from their lips. (7:28).
Cut off your hair and throw it away. Raise up a lamentation on the barren heights, for the LORD has rejected and forsaken the generation of His wrath.’ (7:29).
For the people of Judah have done evil in My sight, declares the LORD. They have set up their abominations in the house that bears My Name, and so have defiled it. (7:30).
They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom so they could burn their sons and daughters in the fire — something I never commanded, nor did it even enter My mind. (7:31).

So behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth and the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter. For they will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no more room. (7:32).
The corpses of this people will become food for the birds of the air and the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one to scare them away. (7:33).
I will remove from the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem the sounds of joy and gladness and the voices of the bride and bridegroom, for the land will become a wasteland.” (7:34).
crossRefs: 1 Samuel 4:10-11: The ark is captured and Eli's sons killed, the ruin of Shiloh that Jeremiah points back to.
Psalm 78:58-64: God abandons the dwelling at Shiloh and gives His people to the sword.
Matthew 21:12-13: Jesus clears the temple and quotes the den of robbers line from 7:11.
Leviticus 18:21: The statute forbidding a man to give any of his children to Molech, the law Topheth breaks.
2 Kings 23:10: Josiah defiles Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom so no one can burn a son or daughter there.

translationNotes.term: Topheth and the Valley of Ben-hinnom
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: תֹּפֶת (topheth) - Hebrew: גֵּיא בֶן־הִנֹּם (ge ven-hinnom)
translationNotes.note: A ravine running along the south and west sides of Jerusalem, just outside the walls, with a burning place called Topheth in it. What happened there is stated flatly in 7:31: they burned their sons and daughters in the fire. Leviticus 18:21 and 20:2-5 set death as the penalty for it, 2 Kings 16:3 and 21:6 record two kings of Judah doing it, and 2 Kings 23:10 records Josiah wrecking the site so it could not be used again.

translationNotes.original: Hebrew: גֵּי הִנֹּם (ge hinnom) - Greek: γέεννα (geenna)
translationNotes.note: Valley of Hinnom in Hebrew becomes Gehenna in Greek. It is the word Jesus uses eleven times in the Gospels for hell, in Matthew 5:22, 5:29, 5:30, 10:28, 18:9, 23:15, 23:33, Mark 9:43, 9:45, 9:47, and Luke 12:5. When He names it, He is naming a real ravine outside Jerusalem where children were burned.

A goddess worshipped by whole households in Judah. Verse 18 lays out the division of labour: the children gather firewood, the fathers kindle it, the women knead dough for her cakes, and drink offerings are poured out. Queen of heaven is the standing title of Ishtar in Mesopotamian texts. The practice comes back in 44:17-19, where the women in Egypt defend it to Jeremiah's face.

The sanctuary town about twenty miles (32 km) north of Jerusalem in Ephraim, where the tabernacle stood through the period of the judges and where Samuel grew up. It was the national worship centre for generations before Jerusalem was. It was destroyed after the ark was captured, which is why 7:12-14 uses it: the argument is that a sanctuary God had chosen was already levelled once.

Not a place where robbery is done but the cave a bandit runs back to afterward. The charge in 7:9-11 is that people were murdering, stealing, swearing falsely and burning incense to Baal, then coming to the temple as a safe house.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jeremiah stands at the temple gate and tells Judah to reform their ways and stop trusting in false security; God warns that because they worship idols, commit injustice, and ignore his prophets, he will destroy the temple and the land as he did Shiloh, and fill the Valley of Ben Hinnom with their dead.

headings.text: Jeremiah’s Message at the Temple Gate

stories.title: 🕍 Jeremiah 8
summaryBullets: “At that time,” declares the LORD, “the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of the officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the people of Jerusalem will be removed from their graves. (8:1).

They will be exposed to the sun and moon, and to all the host of heaven which they have loved, served, followed, consulted, and worshiped. Their bones will not be gathered up or buried, but will become like dung lying on the ground. (8:2).
And wherever I have banished them, the remnant of this evil family will choose death over life,” declares the LORD of Hosts. (8:3).
So you are to tell them this is what the LORD says: “Do men fall and not get up again? Does one turn away and not return? (8:4).
Why then have these people turned away? Why does Jerusalem always turn away? They cling to deceit; they refuse to return. (8:5).
I have listened and heard; they do not speak what is right. No one repents of his wickedness, asking, ‘What have I done?’ Everyone has pursued his own course like a horse charging into battle. (8:6).
Even the stork in the sky knows her appointed seasons. The turtledove, the swift, and the thrush keep their time of migration, but My people do not know the requirements of the LORD. (8:7).
How can you say, ‘We are wise, and the Law of the LORD is with us,’ when in fact the lying pen of the scribes has produced a deception? (8:8).
The wise will be put to shame; they will be dismayed and trapped. Since they have rejected the word of the LORD, what wisdom do they really have? (8:9).

Therefore I will give their wives to other men and their fields to new owners. For from the least of them to the greatest, all are greedy for gain; from prophet to priest, all practice deceit. (8:10).
They dress the wound of the daughter of My people with very little care, saying, ‘Peace, peace,’ when there is no peace at all. (8:11).

Are they ashamed of the abomination they have committed? No, they have no shame at all; they do not even know how to blush. So they will fall among the fallen; when I punish them, they will collapse, says the LORD. (8:12).
I will take away their harvest, declares the LORD. There will be no grapes on the vine, nor figs on the tree, and even the leaf will wither. Whatever I have given them will be lost to them.” (8:13).

Why are we just sitting here? Gather together, let us flee to the fortified cities and perish there, for the LORD our God has doomed us. He has given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD. (8:14).
We hoped for peace, but no good has come, for a time of healing, but there was only terror. (8:15).

The snorting of enemy horses is heard from Dan. At the sound of the neighing of mighty steeds, the whole land quakes. They come to devour the land and everything in it, the city and all who dwell in it. (8:16).
“For behold, I will send snakes among you, vipers that cannot be charmed, and they will bite you,” declares the LORD. (8:17).
My sorrow is beyond healing; my heart is faint within me. (8:18).

Listen to the cry of the daughter of my people from a land far away: “Is the LORD no longer in Zion? Is her King no longer there?” “Why have they provoked Me to anger with their carved images, with their worthless foreign idols?” (8:19).
“The harvest has passed, the summer has ended, but we have not been saved.” (8:20).
For the brokenness of the daughter of my people I am crushed. I mourn; horror has gripped me. (8:21).
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is no physician there? Why then has the health of the daughter of my people not been restored? (8:22).
crossRefs: 2 Kings 23:4-6: Josiah burns the vessels of Baal and scatters their dust on graves, the reverse of the desecration in 8:1-2.
Deuteronomy 4:19: The command not to bow to the sun, moon and host of heaven, the worship named in 8:2.
Genesis 37:25: A caravan carries balm and spices down from Gilead, the trade behind the question in 8:22.
Jeremiah 6:13-15: The same words about greedy prophets and priests who cry peace where there is no peace.
Isaiah 1:3: The ox knows its owner but Israel does not know, the reproach 8:7 makes with migrating birds.

translationNotes.term: Bones brought out of the graves
translationNotes.note: Judeans were buried in rock-cut family tombs, and to be gathered to your fathers meant your bones ended up in the same chamber as theirs. Dragging bones out and leaving them spread on the ground under the sun and stars, as 8:1-2 describes, was the worst thing that could be done to a corpse, and it turns the objects they worshipped into their exposure.

translationNotes.term: The lying pen of the scribes
translationNotes.original: Hebrew: עֵט שֶׁקֶר סֹפְרִים (et sheqer sopherim)
translationNotes.note: Scribes were the men who copied and taught the law; the pen is a cut reed. The charge in 8:8 is that the professionals who handled the text produced a false one, so people could claim to have the law of the LORD and be holding a lie.

An aromatic resin tapped from trees in Gilead, the highlands east of the Jordan, and traded as a healing salve and a luxury good. Genesis 37:25 has it moving down the caravan road with Joseph, and 46:11 sends Egypt to Gilead for it. It was the standard remedy of the region, so the question in 8:22 is asking why the ordinary cure is not working.

Israel sits on the land bridge between Africa and Eurasia, and hundreds of millions of birds funnel over it twice a year. Anyone living there watched the migration arrive and leave on schedule. That is the force of 8:7: the birds keep an appointment they were never taught.

stories.keyTakeaway: The Lord promises to expose the bones of Judah's dead and declares that the people will not repent despite knowing what is right; they claim wisdom while rejecting God's word, and judgment comes as enemy horses approach and the harvest passes without salvation.

stories.title: 💧 Jeremiah 9
summaryBullets: Oh, that my head were a spring of water, and my eyes a fountain of tears! I would weep day and night over the slain daughter of my people. (9:1).
If only I had a traveler’s lodge in the wilderness, I would abandon my people and depart from them, for they are all adulterers, a crowd of faithless people. (9:2).
“They bend their tongues like bows; lies prevail over truth in the land. For they proceed from evil to evil, and they do not take Me into account,” declares the LORD. (9:3).
“Let everyone guard against his neighbor; do not trust any brother, for every brother deals craftily, and every friend spreads slander. (9:4).
Each one betrays his friend; no one tells the truth. They have taught their tongues to lie; they wear themselves out committing iniquity. (9:5).
You dwell in the midst of deception; in their deceit they refuse to know Me,” declares the LORD. (9:6).
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Behold, I will refine them and test them, for what else can I do because of the daughter of My people? (9:7).
Their tongues are deadly arrows; they speak deception. With his mouth a man speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he sets a trap for him. (9:8).
Should I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this?” (9:9).

I will take up a weeping and wailing for the mountains, a dirge over the wilderness pasture, for they have been scorched so no one passes through, and the lowing of cattle is not heard. Both the birds of the air and the beasts have fled; they have gone away. (9:10).
“And I will make Jerusalem a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals; and I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, without inhabitant.” (9:11).

Who is the man wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, that he may explain it? Why is the land destroyed and scorched like a desert, so no one can pass through it? (9:12).
And the LORD answered, “It is because they have forsaken My law, which I set before them; they have not walked in it or obeyed My voice. (9:13).
Instead, they have followed the stubbornness of their hearts and gone after the Baals, as their fathers taught them.” (9:14).
Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I will feed this people wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink. (9:15).
I will scatter them among the nations that neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send a sword after them until I have finished them off.” (9:16).
This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Take note, and summon the wailing women; send for the most skillful among them. (9:17).
Let them come quickly and take up a lament over us, that our eyes may overflow with tears, and our eyelids may gush with water. (9:18).
For the sound of wailing is heard from Zion: ‘How devastated we are! How great is our shame! For we have abandoned the land because our dwellings have been torn down.’” (9:19).
Now, O women, hear the word of the LORD. Open your ears to the word of His mouth. Teach your daughters to wail, and one another to lament. (9:20).
For death has climbed in through our windows; it has entered our fortresses to cut off the children from the streets, the young men from the town squares. (9:21).
Declare that this is what the LORD says: “The corpses of men will fall like dung upon the open field, like newly cut grain behind the reaper, with no one to gather it.” (9:22).
This is what the LORD says: “Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the wealthy man in his riches. (9:23).

But let him who boasts boast in this, that he understands and knows Me, that I am the LORD, who exercises loving devotion, justice and righteousness on the earth — for I delight in these things,” declares the LORD. (9:24).
“Behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will punish all who are circumcised only in the flesh— (9:25).

Egypt, Judah, Edom, Ammon, Moab, and all the inhabitants of the desert who clip the hair of their temples. For all these nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.” (9:26).
crossRefs: Jeremiah 5:1-5: The search of Jerusalem's streets for one man who does justice, the finding behind 9:2-6.
2 Chronicles 35:25: Jeremiah composes laments for Josiah and the singers keep them, the trade the wailing women of 9:17 belong to.
1 Corinthians 1:31: Paul writes that the one who boasts should boast in the Lord, taking up 9:24.
Deuteronomy 10:16: Circumcise the foreskin of your heart, the phrase 9:26 turns into an indictment.
Leviticus 26:33: Scattering among the nations with the sword drawn after them, the sentence pronounced in 9:16.

translationNotes.note: Professional mourners, a paid trade. A family hired them to lead the funeral lament, and they trained their daughters in it, which is what 9:20 means by teaching the dirge. They appear again in Matthew 9:23, where the flute players and the crowd are already at work in Jairus's house before the girl has been buried.

Circumcision was the physical sign of the covenant, cut into every Israelite male on the eighth day. Verses 25-26 list Egypt, Edom, Ammon, Moab and the desert tribes, who practised the cutting too, and then puts Israel in the list. The point is that Judah has the mark on the body and not on the will.

The verb means to praise loudly or to make a public claim about yourself. Verses 23-24 rule out the three things a man in the ancient world would advertise, wisdom, strength and wealth, and leave one thing worth advertising, knowing the LORD. Paul quotes the line twice, in 1 Corinthians 1:31 and 2 Corinthians 10:17.

Verses 10 and 19 picture the nation as a camp being struck. Tent cloth was woven from black goat hair, the ropes were twisted from hair or flax, and the poles were carried. A tent with its cords cut and its poles gone is a household that cannot be put back up anywhere, which is what exile meant in practice.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jeremiah grieves over Judah's deception and unfaithfulness, reporting the Lord's decision to refine them through judgment - scattering them among nations, making their land desolate, and calling wailing women to mourn their ruin. The Lord warns against boasting in wisdom or strength, and declares that all nations, including Judah, will be punished for being uncircumcised in heart.

stories.title: 💧 Jeremiah 10
summaryBullets: Hear the word that the LORD speaks to you, O house of Israel. (10:1).
This is what the LORD says: “Do not learn the ways of the nations or be terrified by the signs in the heavens, though the nations themselves are terrified by them. (10:2).
For the customs of the peoples are worthless; they cut down a tree from the forest; it is shaped with a chisel by the hands of a craftsman. (10:3).
They adorn it with silver and gold and fasten it with hammer and nails, so that it will not totter. (10:4).
Like scarecrows in a cucumber patch, their idols cannot speak. They must be carried because they cannot walk. Do not fear them, for they can do no harm, and neither can they do any good.” (10:5).
There is none like You, O LORD. You are great, and Your name is mighty in power. (10:6).
Who would not fear You, O King of nations? This is Your due. For among all the wise men of the nations, and in all their kingdoms, there is none like You. (10:7).
But they are altogether senseless and foolish, instructed by worthless idols made of wood! (10:8).
Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz — the work of a craftsman from the hands of a goldsmith. Their clothes are blue and purple, all fashioned by skilled workers. (10:9).
But the LORD is the true God; He is the living God and eternal King. The earth quakes at His wrath, and the nations cannot endure His indignation. (10:10).
Thus you are to tell them: “These gods, who have made neither the heavens nor the earth, will perish from this earth and from under these heavens.” (10:11).
The LORD made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding. (10:12).

When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; He causes the clouds to rise from the ends of the earth. He generates the lightning with the rain and brings forth the wind from His storehouses. (10:13).
Every man is senseless and devoid of knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. For his molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them. (10:14).
They are worthless, a work to be mocked. In the time of their punishment they will perish. (10:15).
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for He is the Maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of His inheritance— the LORD of Hosts is His name. (10:16).
Gather up your belongings from this land, you who live under siege. (10:17).
For this is what the LORD says: “Behold, at this time I will sling out the inhabitants of the land and bring distress upon them so that they may be captured.” (10:18).
Woe to me because of my brokenness; my wound is grievous! But I said, “This is truly my sickness, and I must bear it.” (10:19).
My tent is destroyed, and all its ropes are snapped. My sons have departed from me and are no more. I have no one left to pitch my tent or set up my curtains. (10:20).
For the shepherds have become senseless; they do not seek the LORD. Therefore they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered. (10:21).
Listen! The sound of a report is coming — a great commotion from the land to the north. It will make the cities of Judah a desolation, a haunt for jackals. (10:22).
I know, O LORD, that a man’s way is not his own; no one who walks directs his own steps. (10:23).
Correct me, O LORD, but only with justice — not in Your anger, or You will bring me to nothing. (10:24).

Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not acknowledge You, and on the families that do not call on Your name. For they have devoured Jacob; they have consumed him and finished him off; they have devastated his homeland. (10:25).
crossRefs: Isaiah 44:9-20: A craftsman cuts down a tree, burns half of it for warmth and bows down to what is left.
Psalm 115:4-8: Idols with mouths that cannot speak and eyes that cannot see, and makers who become like them.
Deuteronomy 4:15-19: The command against making any carved likeness, and against worshipping sun, moon and stars.
Habakkuk 2:18-19: A woe on the man who tells a block of wood to wake up, an image plated in gold with no breath in it.
Psalm 79:6-7: Nearly the same sentence as 10:25, asking God to pour out wrath on nations that do not know Him.

translationNotes.note: Verses 3-5 give the trade steps in order: timber cut in the forest, shaped with a chisel, overlaid with hammered silver and gold, then fastened upright with hammer and nails so it cannot fall over. The nails are the detail that lands. The thing has to be fixed in place because it cannot stand by itself, and 10:5 finishes the thought: it cannot walk, so it must be carried.

Babylonian religion ran on celestial omens; eclipses, planetary positions and lunar haloes were read as state warnings by a professional priesthood, and the records of it survive in cuneiform. Verse 2 tells Judah not to be terrified by them, which is a direct instruction about the culture the exiles were about to live inside.

Two sources of imported metal named in 10:9. Silver came in from Tarshish, a distant western trading destination reached by sea, and gold from Uphaz. The verse is listing an idol's bill of materials from the far ends of the trade network, and then the craftsman and the dyer who finish it.

translationNotes.term: The tent struck and the cords cut
translationNotes.note: Verse 20 shifts from idols to the speaker's own household. Tent poles broken and the ropes snapped means there is nothing left to pitch, and the following line says the children are gone. It is the picture of a family that cannot even move on as refugees.

stories.keyTakeaway: The LORD warns Israel not to imitate the nations' worthless idol-making practices and declares his own supremacy as the living God who made all things; Jeremiah laments the coming destruction from the north and prays for measured discipline rather than full divine wrath.

stories.title: 📜 Jeremiah 11
summaryBullets: This is the word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD: (11:1).
“Listen to the words of this covenant and tell them to the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. (11:2).
You must tell them that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is the man who does not obey the words of this covenant, (11:3).

which I commanded your forefathers when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying, ‘Obey Me, and do everything I command you, and you will be My people, and I will be your God.’ (11:4).
This was in order to establish the oath I swore to your forefathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is to this day.” “Amen, LORD,” I answered. (11:5).
Then the LORD said to me, “Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, saying: Hear the words of this covenant and carry them out. (11:6).
For from the time I brought your fathers out of the land of Egypt until today, I strongly warned them again and again, saying, ‘Obey My voice.’ (11:7).

Yet they would not obey or incline their ears, but each one followed the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought on them all the curses of this covenant I had commanded them to follow but they did not keep.” (11:8).
And the LORD told me, “There is a conspiracy among the men of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. (11:9).

They have returned to the sins of their forefathers who refused to obey My words. They have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken the covenant I made with their fathers. (11:10).
Therefore this is what the LORD says: ‘I am about to bring upon them a disaster that they cannot escape. They will cry out to Me, but I will not listen to them. (11:11).

Then the cities of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to which they have been burning incense, but these gods certainly will not save them in their time of disaster. (11:12).
Your gods are indeed as numerous as your cities, O Judah; the altars of shame you have set up— the altars to burn incense to Baal— are as many as the streets of Jerusalem.’ (11:13).
As for you, do not pray for these people. Do not raise up a cry or a prayer on their behalf, for I will not be listening when they call out to Me in their time of disaster. (11:14).
What right has My beloved in My house, having carried out so many evil schemes? Can consecrated meat avert your doom? When you are wicked, then you rejoice. (11:15).
The LORD once called you a flourishing olive tree, beautiful with well-formed fruit. But with a mighty roar He will set it on fire, and its branches will be consumed. (11:16).

The LORD of Hosts, who planted you, has decreed disaster against you on account of the evil that the house of Israel and the house of Judah have brought upon themselves, provoking Me to anger by burning incense to Baal.” (11:17).
And the LORD informed me, so I knew. Then You showed me their deeds. (11:18).

For I was like a gentle lamb led to slaughter; I did not know that they had plotted against me: “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, that his name may be remembered no more.” (11:19).
O LORD of Hosts, who judges righteously, who examines the heart and mind, let me see Your vengeance upon them, for to You I have committed my cause. (11:20).
Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the people of Anathoth who are seeking your life and saying, “You must not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand.” (11:21).
So this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “I will punish them. Their young men will die by the sword, their sons and daughters by famine. (11:22).
There will be no remnant, for I will bring disaster on the people of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.” (11:23).
crossRefs: Exodus 19:5-6: The covenant terms at Sinai, obey My voice and keep My covenant, which 11:4 quotes back.
Deuteronomy 27:15-26: The curses recited on Mount Ebal, each answered by the people with Amen, as in 11:5.
Deuteronomy 11:26-28: The blessing and the curse set before Israel for obeying or not obeying.
Joshua 21:17-18: Anathoth listed among the towns given to the priests, which is why Jeremiah's enemies in 11:21 are his own kin.
Isaiah 53:7: A lamb led to the slaughter that does not open its mouth, the image Jeremiah uses of himself in 11:19.

translationNotes.note: The word means let it stand, and in Deuteronomy 27 it is the legally binding response the whole nation shouted back after each curse was read aloud. When Jeremiah answers Amen in 11:5, he is taking the position of a witness confirming the terms of a contract, not closing a prayer.

Not a foundry for making iron but a smelting furnace hot enough to work it, the hottest thing an Israelite could name. The same phrase for Egypt appears in Deuteronomy 4:20 and 1 Kings 8:51, so 11:4 is invoking a stock description of the slavery they came out of.

An olive takes years to come into bearing and then produces for centuries, so it is the picture of a long, secure investment. Verse 16 gives Judah that name and then sets it on fire with a roar, ruining in an afternoon what took generations to grow.

translationNotes.term: Do not pray for this people
translationNotes.note: Repeated in 7:16, 11:14 and 14:11. It is a sentence passed on one generation at one point in a specific case, closing off intercession in that instance. It is not a rule about prayer in general, and Jeremiah goes on praying elsewhere in the book, in 14:19-22 and 32:16-25.

stories.keyTakeaway: God tells Jeremiah to proclaim the covenant terms to Judah and Jerusalem, warning that both Israel and Judah have broken the covenant by pursuing other gods, and that disaster will come upon them; Jeremiah also learns that the men of Anathoth are plotting to kill him, and God promises to punish them.

stories.title: 📜 Jeremiah 12
summaryBullets: Righteous are You, O LORD, when I plead before You. Yet about Your judgments I wish to contend with You: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all the faithless live at ease? (12:1).
You planted them, and they have taken root. They have grown and produced fruit. You are ever on their lips, but far from their hearts. (12:2).
But You know me, O LORD; You see me and test my heart toward You. Drag away the wicked like sheep to the slaughter and set them apart for the day of carnage. (12:3).

How long will the land mourn and the grass of every field be withered? Because of the evil of its residents, the animals and birds have been swept away, for the people have said, “He cannot see what our end will be.” (12:4).
“If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how can you compete with horses? If you stumble in a peaceful land, how will you do in the thickets of the Jordan? (12:5).
Even your brothers— your own father’s household— even they have betrayed you; even they have cried aloud against you. Do not trust them, though they speak well of you. (12:6).
I have forsaken My house; I have abandoned My inheritance. I have given the beloved of My soul into the hands of her enemies. (12:7).
My inheritance has become to Me like a lion in the forest. She has roared against Me; therefore I hate her. (12:8).
Is not My inheritance to Me like a speckled bird of prey with other birds of prey circling against her? Go, gather all the beasts of the field; bring them to devour her. (12:9).
Many shepherds have destroyed My vineyard; they have trampled My plot of ground. They have turned My pleasant field into a desolate wasteland. (12:10).
They have made it a desolation; desolate before Me, it mourns. All the land is laid waste, but no man takes it to heart. (12:11).
Over all the barren heights in the wilderness the destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the earth to the other. No flesh has peace. (12:12).
They have sown wheat but harvested thorns. They have exhausted themselves to no avail. Bear the shame of your harvest because of the fierce anger of the LORD.” (12:13).

This is what the LORD says: “As for all My evil neighbors who attack the inheritance that I bequeathed to My people Israel, I am about to uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them. (12:14).
But after I have uprooted them, I will once again have compassion on them and return each one to his inheritance and to his land. (12:15).

And if they will diligently learn the ways of My people and swear by My name, saying, ‘As surely as the LORD lives’— just as they once taught My people to swear by Baal— then they will be established among My people. (12:16).
But if they will not obey, then I will uproot that nation; I will uproot it and destroy it, declares the LORD.” (12:17).
crossRefs: Psalm 73:1-14: Asaph sees the wicked prospering at their ease and nearly loses his footing.
Job 21:7-15: Job asks why the wicked live on, grow old and increase in power.
Habakkuk 1:13: Habakkuk asks how God can watch treachery in silence while the wicked swallow the righteous.
Deuteronomy 32:9: The LORD's portion is His people and Jacob His allotted inheritance, the language behind My heritage in 12:7-9.
Amos 1:3-15: Oracles against the same neighbouring nations that 12:14-17 says will be uprooted and then replanted.

translationNotes.note: The proverb in 12:5 is drawn from two escalations a traveller would understand. If footmen outrun you now, horses will bury you; if you stumble in open, safe country, you will not survive the thickets along the Jordan. The thickets were the dense scrub of the river floodplain, known for lions, named again in 49:19 and 50:44.

The word for an inherited landholding, the family plot that could not be sold off permanently under Leviticus 25:23. Applied to the nation in 12:7-9, it makes the loss a property loss: God is describing His own inheritance abandoned and left to scavengers.

Verse 9 describes a bird whose markings do not match the flock, so the rest of the birds gather to drive it off and tear at it. Verse 9 then calls the wild beasts in to the meal. The picture is of a nation set on by its own neighbours.

Verses 14-17 name the surrounding peoples who had seized Judean land. The promise is two-sided and stated in the same breath: uprooted first, then brought back, and if they learn to swear by the LORD's name they will be built up among His people. The same nations get chapter-length oracles in 48 and 49.

stories.keyTakeaway: Jeremiah protests to the Lord that wicked people prosper while the land withers, then receives a warning that his own relatives have betrayed him and assurance that God will judge both Judah and the nations around them, though those who learn God's ways may be restored.

stories.title: 📜 Jeremiah 13
summaryBullets: This is what the LORD said to me: “Go and buy yourself a linen loincloth and put it around your waist, but do not let it touch water.” (13:1).
So I bought a loincloth in accordance with the word of the LORD, and I put it around my waist. (13:2).
Then the word of the LORD came to me a second time: (13:3).
“Take the loincloth that you bought and are wearing, and go at once to Perath and hide it there in a crevice of the rocks.” (13:4).
So I went and hid it at Perath, as the LORD had commanded me. (13:5).
Many days later the LORD said to me, “Arise, go to Perath, and get the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there.” (13:6).
So I went to Perath and dug up the loincloth, and I took it from the place where I had hidden it. But now it was ruined— of no use at all. (13:7).
Then the word of the LORD came to me: (13:8).
“This is what the LORD says: In the same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem. (13:9).

These evil people, who refuse to listen to My words, who follow the stubbornness of their own hearts, and who go after other gods to serve and worship them, they will be like this loincloth — of no use at all. (13:10).

For just as a loincloth clings to a man’s waist, so I have made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to Me, declares the LORD, so that they might be My people for My renown and praise and glory. But they did not listen. (13:11).

Therefore you are to tell them that this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘Every wineskin shall be filled with wine.’ And when they reply, ‘Don’t we surely know that every wineskin should be filled with wine?’ (13:12).

then you are to tell them that this is what the LORD says: ‘I am going to fill with drunkenness all who live in this land— the kings who sit on David’s throne, the priests, the prophets, and all the people of Jerusalem. (13:13).
I will smash them against one another, fathers and sons alike, declares the LORD. I will allow no mercy or pity or compassion to keep Me from destroying them.’” (13:14).
Listen and give heed. Do not be arrogant, for the LORD has spoken. (13:15).
Give glory to the LORD your God before He brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the dusky mountains. You wait for light, but He turns it into deep gloom and thick darkness. (13:16).
But if you do not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride. My eyes will overflow with tears, because the LORD’s flock has been taken captive. (13:17).
Say to the king and to the queen mother: “Take a lowly seat, for your glorious crowns have fallen from your heads.” (13:18).
The cities of the Negev have been shut tight, and no one can open them. All Judah has been carried into exile, wholly taken captive. (13:19).
Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock entrusted to you, the sheep that were your pride? (13:20).
What will you say when He sets over you close allies whom you yourself trained? Will not pangs of anguish grip you, as they do a woman in labor? (13:21).
And if you ask yourself, “Why has this happened to me?” It is because of the magnitude of your iniquity that your skirts have been stripped off and your body has been exposed. (13:22).
Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots? Neither are you able to do good — you who are accustomed to doing evil. (13:23).
“I will scatter you like chaff driven by the desert wind. (13:24).
This is your lot, the portion I have measured to you,” declares the LORD, “because you have forgotten Me and trusted in falsehood. (13:25).
So I will pull your skirts up over your face, that your shame may be seen. (13:26).

Your adulteries and lustful neighings, your shameless prostitution on the hills and in the fields — I have seen your detestable acts. Woe to you, O Jerusalem! How long will you remain unclean?” (13:27).
crossRefs: Exodus 28:39-43: Linen is the fabric prescribed for priests, including the undergarments worn next to the skin.
Exodus 19:5-6: Israel called a kingdom of priests and a holy nation, the closeness the clinging loincloth pictures in 13:11.
2 Kings 24:8-15: Jehoiachin and his mother taken to Babylon, the pair told to come down from their thrones in 13:18.
Deuteronomy 8:11-14: The warning that plenty breeds forgetting and pride, the charge behind 13:15-17.
Isaiah 47:2-3: Skirts lifted and nakedness uncovered as the shaming of a captured city, the same image as 13:22-26.

translationNotes.note: A long strip of cloth wound round the waist and between the legs, worn against the skin under everything else. Linen was the priestly fabric, prescribed in Exodus 28:42 for exactly this garment.
